conflicts.description: The record states no known drug allergies -- given on the intake form on 2025-09-12 and again to urgent care on 2026-05-19 -- yet a rash is documented following amoxicillin on both courses. The allergy record has never been revised.
The 2026-05-19 amoxicillin prescription was issued at urgent care by a clinician who did not have access to the patient's records, so the September 2025 rash was not available to the prescriber.
The patient has twice recorded an intention to raise the rash with a clinician but has not done so; it was specifically not mentioned at the 2026-06-09 GP appointment.

patterns_to_raise.observation: A rash of the same description appeared on two separate occasions, each within a few days of starting amoxicillin, and each resolved roughly three days after the antibiotic was stopped. First course started 2025-09-12, rash 2025-09-17, resolved 2025-09-23. Second course started 2026-05-19, rash 2026-05-22, resolved 2026-05-27. On the first occasion the patient attributed it to a new laundry detergent; on the second they ruled that out, the same brand having been in use for eight months, and offered no alternative explanation.
patterns_to_raise.why_it_matters: No drug allergy is recorded, and amoxicillin was prescribed again eight months after the first episode by a clinician without access to the earlier record. The two episodes were written eight months apart, in different words, and the patient has never connected them.

patterns_to_raise.observation: Migraine frequency moves inversely with propranolol adherence. On 20mg the patient averaged about two migraines a month. In the 21 days off it (2026-04-06 to 2026-04-27) they had five, including three in five days. After restarting, frequency returned to about two a month, rose to four in June 2026, and settled to two a month after the increase to 40mg on 2026-07-07.
patterns_to_raise.why_it_matters: An unplanned discontinuation produced a clean natural experiment, which the patient reported themselves on 2026-06-09.

patterns_to_raise.observation: Reported fatigue tracks propranolol dose. It began three days after starting 20mg (2026-01-16), was described as a persistent baseline through February and March, lifted within four days of stopping (2026-04-10), returned within a week of restarting (2026-05-04), and worsened again after the increase to 40mg (2026-07-15).
patterns_to_raise.why_it_matters: The patient has raised the fatigue as their main complaint about treatment and wants to know whether it is unavoidable.

patterns_to_raise.observation: The patient has repeatedly noted that migraines tend to follow a stretch of poor sleep by one to two days, and that quieter, better-slept periods coincided with fewer attacks.
patterns_to_raise.why_it_matters: This is the patient's own observation across several months rather than a measured association.
